name: Qatar
genZNote: Qatar is a country roughly the size of a small Indian state that hosted the entire FIFA World Cup 2022 — natural gas wealth turned a small peninsula into one of the highest GDP-per-capita nations on Earth in a single generation.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: A small peninsula extending into the Persian Gulf from the Arabian Peninsula, bordered only by Saudi Arabia by land.
Predominantly flat, arid desert terrain with a hot climate and very limited fresh water and arable land.
The capital, Doha, is home to a rapidly developed, modern skyline built largely on natural gas wealth.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: Arabic is the official language; Islam is the state religion, and traditional Bedouin and Gulf Arab customs remain culturally significant.
One of the highest ratios of foreign expatriate workers to citizens in the world, with expatriates forming the large majority of the population.
Traditional falconry, dhow sailing, and pearl-diving heritage remain culturally important despite the country's rapid modernisation.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: An absolute monarchy (emirate) ruled by the Al Thani family, with the Emir as head of state; a partially elected Shura Council advises on legislation.
One of the wealthiest countries in the world by per-capita income, driven almost entirely by natural gas exports.
Hosted the 2022 FIFA World Cup, the first in the Middle East, involving massive infrastructure investment.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: A major global player in energy diplomacy as one of the world's largest exporters of liquefied natural gas (LNG).
Home to the influential Al Jazeera media network and hosts a major US military base (Al Udeid), giving it significant regional diplomatic weight.
Recovered from a 2017-2021 diplomatic blockade by several Gulf neighbours, after which relations were restored.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India and Qatar share a 'Strategic Partnership', with Qatar being a major supplier of liquefied natural gas (LNG) to India.
Home to a large Indian expatriate community, one of the largest expatriate groups in Qatar, contributing significantly to remittances.
Cooperation has grown in trade, investment, and labour welfare, especially highlighted during World Cup-related infrastructure projects employing many Indian workers.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: One of the world's top exporters of liquefied natural gas (LNG), which underpins its extremely high per-capita income.
Economy is diversifying into finance, sports, tourism, and logistics beyond hydrocarbons.
Sovereign wealth fund (Qatar Investment Authority) is a major global investor across real estate, sports clubs, and technology.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: Hosting the 2022 FIFA World Cup, the first Middle Eastern country to do so.
Being one of the world's largest LNG exporters and having among the highest per-capita incomes globally.
The influential Al Jazeera global news network.
A very large expatriate workforce relative to its citizen population.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Qatar is a small, extremely wealthy Gulf Arab emirate and one of the world's largest LNG exporters, ruled as an absolute monarchy by the Al Thani family.
keyFacts: Absolute monarchy (emirate) ruled by the Al Thani family.
One of the world's top exporters of liquefied natural gas (LNG).
commonConfusion: Qatar's wealth is driven overwhelmingly by natural gas, not oil, distinguishing its economic base from some other Gulf states.

highYieldFacts: Qatar: absolute monarchy (emirate), capital Doha, ruled by Al Thani family.
One of the world's largest LNG exporters; hosted 2022 FIFA World Cup.
India-Qatar: major LNG supplier to India; large Indian expatriate community.
commonTraps: Assuming Qatar's wealth is primarily oil-based — it is primarily natural gas (LNG).
Forgetting Qatar experienced a Gulf diplomatic blockade (2017-2021) before ties were restored.
mustRemember: Qatar: LNG-rich emirate, hosted 2022 World Cup, major India labour/energy partner.

sources.name: Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India — India-Qatar Relations
